assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology to incretin-based therapy is a rare complete arc from hormone biology to a transformative class of drugs for type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefits now documented in large trials. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are all very high.
assessment.attribution: Decisive scientific contributions are credited to Holst (GLP-1 physiology and secretion), Drucker (proglucagon-derived peptides, GLP-2 and GLP-1 biology, receptor action) and Mojsov (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1 peptide). Knudsen's pharmaceutical development is important but is an industrial translation role; the three-person configuration is fair but the Mojsov/Habener-lab credit is debated, and I do not know the full priority record.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of mechanistic work, multiple approved drugs, and large independent outcome trials. Recognition is timely and arguably pressing given the clinical scale.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit for the identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is contested and I have not independently verified the priority record.
Whether the committee prefers to include a drug-development scientist such as Knudsen instead of one of the physiologists.
Long-term safety and durability of effects with chronic use are still accumulating.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific control of activity with millisecond precision. It is a widely used experimental invention that transformed circuit research and is entering clinical use (for example in vision restoration).
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterisation by Nagel, Hegemann and Bamberg, and the neuronal implementation by Boyden and Deisseroth, plus earlier genetic photostimulation by Miesenboeck, make this a classic more-than-three problem. Deisseroth, Nagel and Hegemann is a defensible configuration but leaves out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenboeck, which is a real fairness concern.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and broadly confirmed with enormous independent uptake; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Credit is spread across at least six people and any trio will be disputed.
Medical impact is still early compared with its research impact, relevant for a Medicine prize.
I have not verified exact priority dates for the first neuronal demonstrations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL inhibition established the principle of targeted therapy against a defined oncogenic driver, turning chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal into a manageable chronic disease. The discovery is clear, original and has lasting impact on oncology.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery and kinase program), Druker (clinical proof of concept and development) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a natural trio. The upstream discovery of the BCR-ABL fusion (Rowley, Groffen, Heisterkamp, Witte, Baltimore) is outside the credited list, which weakens a complete story.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature with long-term survival data and global use; recognition is long established and not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the foundational cytogenetic and fusion-gene work is credited elsewhere and whether the prize can be fair without it.
Sawyers' contribution is resistance and follow-on drugs rather than the original discovery, so inclusion is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of tau in neurofibrillary tangles and alpha-synuclein in Lewy bodies and glial inclusions defined the molecular pathology of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease and related disorders. It underpins biomarker development, seed-amplification assays, cryo-EM filament classification and therapeutic programs.
assessment.attribution: Goedert and Spillantini are the central figures for both discoveries and form a clean two-person configuration. Other groups (for example the Lee and Trojanowski or Takeda groups) contributed in parallel and credit is only partly captured by the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by independent groups for two decades; the pathology is stable, though disease-modifying therapies targeting these proteins have not yet succeeded, so patient benefit is still prospective.
uncertainties: Absence of proven disease-modifying therapy limits the translational argument.
Overlap of credit with other groups, and I am relying on memory rather than verification of priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new therapeutic modality, now extending toward autoimmunity. Impact is large and clearly demonstrated.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early CAR design with costimulation), June (clinical translation in leukemia) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer principles and early engineered-cell trials) is plausible, but Eshhar, Kuwana and others contributed early concepts, and the credited list may not map cleanly onto the decisive steps.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature with multiple approved products, though long-term outcomes, toxicity and solid tumor limitations remain.
uncertainties: Priority among Eshhar, Sadelain and June and whether Rosenberg's role is decisive for CAR-T specifically.
Uncertainty over long-term durability and safety.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-frequency deep brain stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus and thalamus transformed treatment of advanced Parkinson's disease and tremor and has been extended to other disorders. It is a clear clinical discovery with lasting impact on patients.
assessment.attribution: The credited name is a single individual, which gives a clean configuration, but the field also owes work to Delong, Bergman and Wichmann on basal ganglia circuitry and to other surgical pioneers; I cannot assess from the supplied data whether Benabid alone is a fair allocation.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of randomized trials and routine clinical use; recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Whether a single laureate is adequate given contributions of basal ganglia circuit researchers.
Mechanism of action of DBS remains incompletely understood.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing produced nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, and validated splice-switching oligonucleotides as a drug class. The mechanistic and clinical story is clear and dramatic.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO design for SMN2) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are a coherent pair. Other contributors, such as Hua and Singh or the SMN gene discoverers (Melki, Lefebvre), may also have claims.
assessment.maturity: Mature enough: approved since 2016, with long-term follow-up and benefit in infants. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Allocation versus those who identified the SMN genes.
Industrial development credit versus academic mechanism credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response, including IRE1, HAC1 splicing and ER-to-nucleus signalling, defined a basic principle of proteostasis with relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. The concept is original and clear.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori carried out the decisive work independently and in complementary steps, giving a natural pair; Ron (eIF2alpha/PERK arm) and others may argue for inclusion.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and fundamental for decades; clinical translation is still developing, which weakens the Medicine link relative to others on the list.
uncertainties: Strength of direct medical impact is moderate.
Potential for an additional contributor (for example the PERK branch).
